subject: Pilot scope & model recommendations for EU/APAC localization use case
messages:
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot scope & model recommendations for EU/APAC localization use case

Quick recap from this morning's call with Susan (Localization Labs) and ops:

- Use case: post-edit assistance + user-facing summarization in customer support workflows. Primary locales: ES (es-ES), FR (fr-FR), DE (de-DE), JP (ja-JP), KR (ko-KR).
- Key constraints: tight latency targets for interactive editor (p95 < 300ms token time), context window ~2k tokens, throughput modest (peak ~10 qps) but unpredictable bursts during mornings EU time.
- Quality priorities: preserve formal register for EU legal snippets (low hallucination tolerance), high fluency for APAC languages.
- Data residency: customer asking for EU data residency for EU traffic; APAC can be in region shared infra.

Immediate asks for internal:
1) Model recommendations and quick bench runs we can show next Wed (04/28).
2) Share the prompt bundles used during call and a short per-locale pilot plan (2 weeks).
3) Outline monitoring/regression checks we will include in the pilot.

I've attached the initial prompt bundle we collected during discovery and the pilot template. Can Aditya propose the model shortlist + initial benchmark? Rishi -- can you add the monitoring checklist and guardrails?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[kim.park@redwood.com]
[Attachment: localize_prompt_set_es_zh_v1.jsonl (prompt set, 28KB)]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-20T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope & model recommendations for EU/APAC localization use case

Thanks Kim — readout below and a couple of tradeoffs to call out. Attaching the quick benchmark HTML export.

Shortlist (initial):
- redwood-7b-quant (multi-lingual, 16-bit quant profile) — best balance for FR/ES/DE for formal/legal tone, strong RLHF alignment on hallucination suppression.
- redwood-3b-int8 (lower cost) — good for JP/KR where latency is priority; expect slight drop on rare legal phrasing.
- open-m3-small (community model) — low latency option for cheap edge testing; likely worse on quality for DE legal text.

Rationale & suggested pilot split:
- Week 1: FR/ES on redwood-7b-quant in eu-west (run 500 prompt samples each, human-in-the-loop for legal snippets).
- Week 2: JP/KR on redwood-3b-int8 in asia-south (focus on latency and fluency).
- Canary: start with FR only, traffic shadow for ES; after 48 hours escalate to 10% live if PQ metrics hold.

Benchmarks delivered: per-locale BLEU/chrF, human pass rate on safety/legal checks, latency p50/p95, token-cost estimates. Link: https://redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/LL-APAC-EU-2027 (internal).

Notes on quantization & quality: the 7b-quant profile we propose preserves FP16-kernel paths for attention and KV cache to avoid tail-regression on long contexts. For 3b-int8 we need to add a short regen step in the pipeline for edge wordpiece instability on JP/KR.

Attachments:
- benchmark_run_20270419.html (summary + per-prompt breakdown)
- MAP-pilot-mpd.xlsx (pilot milestones, metrics, ownership)

Next actions: I will produce the per-prompt prompt-variants (formal vs. neutral) and a short script to compute the automatic similarity/regression metrics. Will share by EOD Monday.

—Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: benchmark_run_20270419.html (report, 120KB)]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-20T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope & model recommendations for EU/APAC localization use case

Good notes — adding monitoring and regression guardrails. Key items we'll include in the pilot (technical):

1) Regression detection: daily auto-eval against our golden prompt set + per-locale human spot checks (10 samples/day). Alert if average pass rate drops >5% week-over-week.
2) Output-level similarity checks: token-level perplexity shift and embedding-similarity delta to detect style/regressions.
3) Fallback policies: circuit-breaker to route to redwood-3b-int8 or open-m3-small if latency p95 > 600ms for >3 minutes; degrade gracefully (shorter context) rather than dropping requests.
4) Audit & retention: for EU-bound traffic we'll enforce EU-region logging and set retention to 30 days unless customer requests otherwise. Include sample retention policy for procurement.

Operational asks: procurement will need the SOW + pricing bands for the two-week pilot and the expanded 3-month pilot. Kimberly — can you confirm whether Localization Labs requires a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) ahead of pilot sign? If so we should attach the standard DPA and the SOC2 summary.

I'll spin up the Redwood Console dashboard template and share the invite for the pilot workspace.

—Rishi
Principal Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: susan@localize.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ops@localize.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot scope & model recommendations for EU/APAC localization use case

Kimberly — thanks for the thorough recap and to Aditya/Rishi for the proposed plan. We are happy to proceed with the narrower pilot you suggested: FR and ES first, then JP/KR next. A few questions before we sign the pilot SOW:

1) Can you confirm EU data residency & that logs for EU traffic will remain in eu-west during the pilot?
2) What is the expected per-token cost for redwood-7b-quant vs redwood-3b-int8 in pilot mode (estimate for ~60k tokens/week)?
3) Who will own human review for legal snippets during week 1 (we can provide 2 reviewers but would like Redwood QA support for calibration).

Please send the SOW + DPA and the sample pilot dashboard. We can target a kickoff for Monday 04/26 if the paperwork is in place.

Best,
Susan Park
Localization Lead | Localization Labs
susan@localize.ai
[Attachment: localization_requirements_summary.pdf (referenced)]
